title: What the page and GitHub rely on

entities.title: GET /auth/me
entities.summary: How the page tells a server from a plain file, and who is signed in.
guarantees: Answers JSON with configured: false when sign-in is not set up.
Otherwise configured: true and user: { login, avatar } for a valid session, or user: null.
entities.compatibility: The page treats anything but a JSON answer with configured: true as no server, so a field may be added; configured and user keep their meaning.

entities.title: /api/github/<path>
entities.summary: GitHub's REST API under the Worker's own address, for the allowed reads.
consumers: index.html (the github adapter, githubApi and ghGet)
guarantees: For a signed-in reader, GET on user, user/repos, repos/<owner>/<repo>, its git/trees/<ref> and its contents/<path> answers as api.github.com would for that reader, query string included.
Accept: application/vnd.github.raw is passed on, so a file can be read raw.
x-ratelimit-remaining and x-ratelimit-reset are passed on.
401 means no session, or a session GitHub no longer accepts.
entities.compatibility: A path the page starts using must be added to ALLOWED in the same change.

entities.title: The sign-in routes and their answers
entities.summary: How the page starts a sign-in and learns how it went.
consumers: index.html (signInUrl, showSignIn and the start of the script)
The GitHub OAuth App, whose registered callback is this route
guarantees: GET /auth/github/start takes return, a path in the app, and private=1 to ask for private repositories.
A sign-in ends at the return path, or with ?signin=denied when the reader cancelled at GitHub, or at /?signin=failed.
POST /auth/sign-out from the app's origin signs out.
entities.compatibility: Moving the callback means registering the new address on the OAuth App first.

entities.title: /api/admin/*
entities.summary: What /admin calls to read and change the crawler's list and settings.
guarantees: GET state answers { user: { name, email }, settings, addresses } with each address's scan state; user is the admin signed in to icelander.net.
PUT settings takes default_interval_minutes (15 to 525600), default_max_stale_minutes, pages_per_scan (1 to 500) and ai_enabled (0 or 1) as whole numbers; anything else is a 400.
POST addresses takes { url, label?, intervalMinutes?, maxStaleMinutes? }, normalizes the URL, answers 201 and queues a first scan, or 409 for an address already listed.

PATCH addresses/<id> changes label, enabled, intervalMinutes or maxStaleMinutes; POST addresses/<id>/rescan queues a scan unless one is queued; DELETE addresses/<id> removes it and everything collected for it.
401 without an icelander.net sign-in, 403 for a user without the role explorer:admin or a change from another origin, 503 when the crawler's bindings are missing.
entities.compatibility: Only /admin uses it, and both are served by the same Worker, so they change together.

sources.symbol: admin API: add, refuse a duplicate, change, rescan, stop and remove an address

entities.title: /api/space
entities.summary: The page's door to what the crawler collected.
guarantees: GET /api/space?url=<address> answers { id, url, kind, label, status, source, scannedAt, stale, paths, staleViews, needsAi, head } for an enabled address, and 404 for any other.
GET /api/space/<id>/files/<path> answers a view file of an enabled address; a path with an empty, . or .. segment, or not ending in .json, is a 400.
POST /api/space/<id>/approach answers { stale, rescanning }, queues a rescan only when the address is stale and not already queued, and only from the explorer's own origin.
entities.compatibility: Fields are only added. paths are the crawler's tree paths; the page reads them as a .cyberspace-explorer tree.

sources.symbol: /api/space: what an explored address has, its view files, nothing for addresses not on the list

entities.title: /crawler
entities.summary: The page the crawler's user agent points site owners to.
guarantees: Answers docs/cyberspace-protocol.md as an HTML page: what the crawler is, how it behaves, how to keep it out and how to cooperate.
entities.compatibility: The URL is in every request the crawler makes, so it never moves.
